title: Philadelphia-area native Steve Tobin brings his art to the region for the first time
summary: Tyler Arboretum invites the public to experience STEVE TOBIN: IN THE LIGHT, a large-scale contemporary sculpture exhibition. The arboretum’s diverse landscapes will feature massive outdoor sculptures by Steve Tobin , an internationally acclaimed artist showing in his native Philadelphia for the first time. Opening Friday, Oct. 16, the exhibition will showcase more than 50 of Tobin's nature-inspired pieces across 15 unique sites throughout the arboretum. Full of movement and color, the sculptures will amplify the natural forms, dynamic forces and layered history of Tyler’s 650-acre landscape. The weekend kickoff will include guided tours, festivities, food and drink to enjoy on Saturday, Oct. 17, and Sunday, Oct. 18. Tyler Arboretum is open daily 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., and exhibition programs and events will be announced throughout the coming year.

title: Christie's Classic Week returns to Paris with rediscovered Boucher and Fragonard masterpieces
summary: From 3 to 5 November, Christie's Classic Week returns to Paris with an exceptional selection of books, paintings, sculptures and works of art celebrating the richness of Europe's artistic heritage. Conceived by Christie's for the great capitals of taste and collecting, namely Paris, London and New York, Classic Week offers stimulating dialogues between periods, styles and artistic disciplines. By presenting each year a fresh journey through centuries of creativity, with a constant focus on quality, Christie's specialists foster exchanges with collectors and enthusiasts while helping to illuminate the history of taste. On 3 November, in a newly conceived format, The Exceptional Sale, L'esprit français explores the very essence of French craftsmanship, from master cabinetmakers and decorative arts to fashion. title: Joseph Bellows Gallery presents Roger Vail's historic hot rod photography series 'Rod & Custom'
summary: Joseph Bellows Gallery presents Roger Vail: Rod & Custom, an exhibition of photographs made at Midwestern raceways in 1967 and 1968. Among Vail’s earliest sustained bodies of work, the series records the hot rod and custom-car culture that developed around regional drag strips during the late 1960s. Vail was drawn not only to the automobiles themselves, but to the broader environment surrounding them. Drivers, spectators, mechanics, girlfriends, machinery, signage, and the improvised architecture of the track all enter into his pictures. The customized cars, with their exaggerated forms, polished surfaces, exposed engines, and hand-built modifications, become part of a larger portrait of American youth culture and its particular combination of ingenuity, performance, competition, and style. title: Christie's Hong Kong Watches presents two dedicated auctions of exceptional horological masterpieces
summary: In celebration of its 40th anniversary in Asia, Christie's announces two live watch auctions this November: The Iconic 40 Watches Evening Sale on 25 November and the Important Watches Sale on 26 November, during Hong Kong Luxury Week. Featuring more than 300 exceptional vintage and contemporary timepieces from leading names including Patek Philippe, Rolex, Audemars Piguet, Cartier, F.P. Journe and Richard Mille, the sales are led by Kronos: Titans of Time Collection, one of the most important single-owner watch collections ever offered by Christie's. With a combined low estimate exceeding HK$330 million, the two auctions represent the highest-ever seasonal total estimate for the watches category in Asia. The sales showcase the artistry, innovation, rarity and craftsmanship that define the pinnacle of horological collecting. Leading the sales is the unprecedented offering of both

title: Laing Art Gallery presents major exhibition exploring the literary roots of Pre-Raphaelite art
summary: Though they are synonymous with taking inspiration from medieval and early Renaissance visual art, the Pre-Raphaelites were also hugely influenced by literature, ranging from Dante Aligheri (1265-1321) and Geoffrey Chaucer (c.1343-1400) to John Keats (1795-1821) and that giant of Victorian poetry, Alfred, Lord Tennyson (1809-1892). Uniquely exploring these connections between Pre-Raphaelite art and poetry, this major exhibition at the Laing Art Gallery will feature over 100 masterpiece paintings, drawings and objects by luminaries of the movement (founded in 1848) by artists such as William Holman Hunt (1827-1910), John Everett Millais (1829-1896), Edward Burne-Jones (1833-1898), Arthur Hughes (1832-1915), and the influential poet-painter Dante Gabriel Rossetti (1828-1882) and poet and designer William Morris (1834-1896). title: AGO reveals highlights from its collection of historical picture frames
summary: The Art Gallery of Ontario (AGO) is home to North America’s largest museum collection of historic picture frames, and this fall the museum invites visitors to discover the artistry that surrounds the art. Opening on October 17, 2026, In Plain Sight: Highlights from the AGO’s Collection of Historic Frames, presents 31 frames dating from the 15 th to early 20th centuries. This exhibition features frames made in England, France, Germany, Spain, Italy and the Netherlands, and is co-curated by Eric Birkle, the AGO’s Marie Zimmermann Curatorial Fellow in European Art; Julia Campbell-Such, the AGO’s Assistant Conservator, Frames; and Adam Harris Levine, the AGO’s Associate Curator of European Art. title: TASCHEN releases expansive 1,356-page visual history of National Geographic photography
summary: There are books you read, books you consult, and books you keep returning to simply because they are beautiful objects. National Geographic: Around the World in 125 Years belongs firmly in the third category. Published by TASCHEN in three substantial hardcover volumes, the set is less a conventional photography book than a visual history of how the world has been seen, documented, interpreted, and sometimes misunderstood since the late 19th century. Across 1,356 pages, it follows National Geographic from its earliest black-and-white imagery through autochromes, Kodachrome, underwater photography, wildlife photography, and the digital age. The geographical structure gives the collection an almost epic sweep. The journey begins in the Americas and Antarctica, continues through Europe and Africa, and concludes in Asia and Oceania. title: First edition Harry Potter brings $400,000 at Heritage Auctions
summary: Before the films, the theme parks and the worldwide phenomenon, there were just 500 hardcover copies. On Oct. 14, one of those first printings of J.K. Rowling’s Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone sold for $400,000 at Heritage Auctions, achieving the second-highest auction price for the title, behind the $471,000 record Heritage established in December 2021. The book led Heritage’s Rare Books Signature® Auction, which realized $2.158 million across 384 lots and participation from 1,077 bidders worldwide. Strong results extended from modern literary landmarks to rare early English Bibles. “Harry Potter’s place in literary history began with an extraordinarily small hardcover printing, most of it destined for public libraries,” says Heritage Auctions Executive Vice President Joe Maddalena. “Collectors recognize how few opportunities there are to own one of those original 500 copies. title: 1959 Gibson Les Paul Brings $781,250 at Heritage
summary: One of the most coveted electric guitars ever made has established a new auction benchmark at Heritage Auctions. An exceptionally preserved 1959 Gibson Les Paul Standard Sunburst sold for $781,250 in the Oct. 15 Vintage Guitars and Musical Instruments Signature® Auction, setting a world auction record for a vintage guitar without celebrity provenance. The result led a $2.15 million auction comprising 201 lots and drawing 848 international bidders, marking a significant achievement for Heritage’s Vintage Guitars & Musical Instruments category. The Les Paul surpassed the previous benchmark of $611,000, paid for a 1958/63 Gibson Explorer at Skinner on Oct. 15, 2006, by $170,250, or approximately 28 percent. “This is a landmark result for vintage guitars and for our department,” says Aaron Piscopo, Director of Vintage Guitars & Musical Instruments at Heritage Auctions. “The 1959 Les Paul Standard has long been one of the most sought-after electric guitars in the world,

title: Exceptional British Modernist artworks saved by Art Fund for South West museums
summary: Art Fund has stepped in to save 22 artworks from the Dartington Hall Collection for the nation, providing an exceptional grant to fund a joint acquisition by The Box, Plymouth, and the Royal Albert Memorial Museum & Art Gallery (RAMM), Exeter. The collection of works by leading British Modernist artists has been acquired in its entirety through a private sale brokered by Phillips ahead of its Modern & Contemporary Art auctions during Frieze Week in London. The collection comprises paintings, works on paper and ceramics by artists central to the history of twentieth-century British art, including Bernard Leach (1887-1979), Ben Nicholson (1894-1982), Winifred Nicholson (1893-1891), Lucie Rie (1902-1995) and Christopher Wood (1901-1930). title: Hudson River Museum acquires Maya Lin's "The Hudson Bight" for permanent collection
summary: The Hudson River Museum announced the acquisition of The Hudson Bight by acclaimed artist, architectural designer, and environmental advocate Maya Lin, recipient of the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor, and the National Medal of Arts. Widely regarded as one of the most influential American artists of her generation, Lin has cultivated a multidisciplinary practice that bridges art, architecture, science, and environmental stewardship. Originally created as the site-specific centerpiece of HRM's acclaimed 2018-19 solo exhibition Maya Lin: A River Is a Drawing, The Hudson Bight transforms scientific data into a single monumental hanging sculpture that reveals the hidden underwater landscape connecting the Hudson River to the Atlantic Ocean. The acquisition secures for the Museum's permanent collection a work by one of the foremost artists of our time and reinforces HRM's commitment to exploring the intersection of art, science, and the environment. title: Éléonore False transforms Les Tanneries into a nocturnal landscape for "Sœur de nuit"
summary: Éléonore False is turning the upper gallery of Les Tanneries into a shifting landscape of shadows, fragments and luminous forms with Sœur de nuit, an immersive exhibition opening October 17, 2026 and continuing through February 28, 2027. The exhibition forms the second half of a two-part project begun with Sœur de jour at the Centre de Création Contemporaine Olivier Debré in Tours. Rather than simply transferring works from one institution to another, False uses the sharply different architecture of Les Tanneries - a former industrial site converted into a contemporary art center - to reconsider how her images, sculptures and textiles inhabit space. At the center of the installation is a large-scale scenographic work also titled Sœur de nuit. Black sequined tulle stretches through the gallery, moving across walls and architectural volumes and dividing the space into a sequence of rooms, thresholds and shifting viewpoints. title: Landmark show includes more than 100 artworks and new scholarship by Edie McKee Harper
summary: The Taft Museum of Art, in partnership with the Charley and Edie Harper Art Studio, presents Edie McKee Harper: Modernist at Play, on view October 17, 2026, through January 24, 2027. This landmark exhibition marks the first solo museum presentation devoted to the work of Edie McKee Harper (1922–2010), a Cincinnati-based artist whose prolific career spanned more than six decades and a remarkable range of media. Accompanied by a comprehensive catalog and new scholarly research, the exhibition brings together more than 100 works offering a long-overdue exploration of the breadth and depth of Harper’s distinctive artistic vision and her lasting contributions to mid-20th century American art and design. Modernist at Play traces Harper’s creative journey through themes she returned to throughout her career: the American landscape, abstraction, storytelling, and the animal world—especially domestic cats. title: Smithsonian National Museum of African Art announces transformative Jack Faxon bequest
summary: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of African Art has announced a donation from former Michigan senator Jack Faxon (1936–2020). The donation includes a bequeathed collection of 100 19th- and 20th-century African artworks that Faxon acquired over the course of his life as well as over $2 million in endowment funds to support the care and development of the museum’s permanent collection, which now includes the Jack Faxon Collection of African Art. The donation is one of the most significant in the museum’s history. “We thank Jack Faxon for this extraordinary gift,” said John K. Lapiana, director of the National Museum of African Art. “Senator Faxon set an example through leadership in the arts and education, and he understood the value that these fields bring to public life. title: Smithsonian's Lemelson Center appoints Joanna K. Garner as New Director
summary: The Smithsonian has appointed Joanna K. Garner, an internationally recognized scholar and leader in educational research, as the Jerome and Dorothy Lemelson Director of the Lemelson Center for the Study of Invention and Innovation at the National Museum of American History. She is the third director in the Lemelson Center’s 30-year history and the first woman to serve in the role. Garner began her new role Tuesday, Sept. 8. She has more than two decades of experience in educational research and cross-sector partnerships across museums, universities, schools and public institutions. Her research has examined how educational and museum experiences can shape people’s identities as inventors and innovators, including how invention education can help people understand their own inventive potential and see themselves as capable of contributing to innovation. “Joanna Garner brings a remarkable combination of scholarship, leadership and critical understanding of the Lemelson Cen

title: Palestine £50 from Fady Nassif Collection brings record $170,800 at Heritage
summary: An exceptionally rare Palestine Currency Board 50 Pounds note from 1929 sold for a record $170,800 to lead Heritage Auctions’ World Paper Money Signature® Auction to $3,268,298 Oct. 14–15, the most ever achieved in a U.S.-based world paper money auction. The results underscored the significance of the Fady Nassif Collection, which brought together rare issued Egyptian and Middle Eastern banknotes alongside material documenting the design and production of currency. The collection was among the auction’s central attractions, with several of its offerings achieving record prices. The Palestine Currency Board 50 Pounds 30.9.1929 Pick 10b PMG Very Fine 30, from the celebrated Fady Nassif Collection, established an auction record for the type and a Heritage record for any banknote from Palestine. title: National Center for Art Research presents JUMP program artists in Sydney, Lisbon and Los Angeles
summary: Emerging Japanese artists present new work at museums in Sydney, Lisbon and Los Angeles through Japan's JUMP program. Supported by the Japanese Government, the JUMP pairs each artist with a Japanese curator and an overseas partner museum. The National Center for Art Research (NCAR), Japan, announces three overseas exhibitions resulting from the JUMP, Global Collaboration Program for Emerging Artists and Curators from Japan, a professional development program organized by the Agency for Cultural Affairs, Government of Japan, the Japan Arts Council, and NCAR to support the international careers of emerging Japanese artists and early-career curators. Over more than eighteen months, three artist-curator teams (seven participants in total) have worked with partner museums in three cities, undertaking research residencies abroad and producing new work based on their findings. title: Kate Newby transforms gallery architecture in new solo exhibition 'Can't find water'
summary: Born in Aotearoa, New Zealand, Kate Newby lives and works in South Texas. For more than twenty years, she has developed a practice that pushes the boundaries of sculpture and blurs the lines between object, architecture, and landscape. Rather than simply occupying a site, her works alter how a place is understood and experienced, taking part in the very experience of inhabiting it. Can’t find water presents a body of recent works by Kate Newby. Following on from her bronze air vents installed at the gallery entrance in 2022, the new sculptures occupy the exhibition space in all its dimensions. New glass windows cut into the walls bring light into previously enclosed spaces, while ceramic forms extend across the walls and from floor to ceiling. Together with suspended glass works, they work their way into the building’s very masonry, altering the architecture itself. title: Van Abbemuseum reimagines its original 1936 architecture in 'Museum as Sundial'
summary: The Van Abbemuseum presents Museum as Sundial, a reorientation of the museum that takes the sundial, one of humanity's oldest technologies for finding direction, as a tool for orientation in the present. Bringing together eleven artists and designers across sculpture, film, architecture, videogame design, sound, performance, performance and live-action role-play, alongside special loans from archives and collections, the exhibition asks how a museum might help us find direction in times of profound change. The starting point is the Van Abbemuseum's original 1936 building, designed in dialogue with the sun. title: From Gothic Futurism to armed letters: Museion hosts first Italian retrospective dedicated to RAMMELLZEE
summary: Museion presents RAMM:ELL:ZEE: TIME:LINE, the only Italian presentation of the first comprehensive European retrospective devoted to RAMMELLZEE (1960–2010). Curated by Hugo Vitrani and Cédric Fauq, with exhibition design by Pascal Rodriguez, the exhibition spans two floors and brings together more than 150 works, the majority never previously shown in Italy, offering an extensive view of the artist’s radical and multifaceted practice. Developed in collaboration with the Palais de Tokyo, Paris, and the Capc Musée d’art contemporain de Bordeaux, TIME:LINE marks the final chapter of a three-part European exhibition project. title: Kunsthuis Syb presents 'Family Album', a group survey on queer kinship and chosen family
summary: Kunsthuis Syb presents Family Album, a group exhibition with newly commissioned and existing works by Ulises Carrión, Sara Sejin Chang (Sara van der Heide), Robert Glück, Hervé Guibert, Tirdad Hashemi, Hetty Huisman, Peter Hujar, Bastienne Kramer, Matthew Lutz-Kinoy, Ugo Rondinone, and Mikołaj Sobczak. The exhibition questions how a domestic atmosphere can be reimagined when traditional family structures are absent or insufficient. The artworks introduce a constellation of friends, companion-lovers, relatives, and ghosts, all of whom form rituals and bonds. title: Hasenkamp opens new art storage facility in the Frankfurt area
summary: Hasenkamp has commenced operations at its new art storage facility in the Frankfurt area. The site offers around 12,000 square metres of storage space and 500 square metres of office space. Around 50 staff members work there. Hasenkamp is thus continuing its long-standing presence in the Rhine-Main region. The Frankfurt branch was previously based in Kelsterbach. With the move to Mörfelden-Walldorf, it is moving into a new building designed specifically to meet the requirements of art logistics. “Frankfurt and the Rhine-Main region are of great importance to our national and international activities. With this new site, we are making a long-term investment in additional capacity, modern infrastructure and the further development of our art logistics,” says Thomas Schneider, managing partner of the Hasenkamp Group. title: Three major exhibitions advance the mission of the Centre for Global Asias
summary: The Vancouver Art Gallery today announced three upcoming exhibitions that bring together extraordinary artistic practices and perspectives from across Asia and its global diasporas. Organized by the Vancouver Art Gallery as an initiative of the Centre for Global Asias, the 2026/2027 exhibition line-up includes the largest exhibition of Iranian modernism in Canada, six decades of artistic innovation in Hong Kong and two ambitious moving-image installations from Filipina Canadian artist, Stephanie Comilang.
